references.text: The previous conquest of Libnah, from which Joshua and Israel departed to attack Lachish
The continuation of the siege of Lachish, where the Lord gave the city into Israel's hand
The king of Lachish is mentioned among the kings whom Joshua and the Israelites defeated
Lachish is mentioned as one of the cities in Judah
King Amaziah fled to Lachish, showing the city's later significance
The Assyrian king Sennacherib sent his army from Lachish to Jerusalem
Libnah is mentioned as one of the camp sites during Israel's wilderness journey
The pattern for taking possession of the promised land by moving from city to city in war
